sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section contains the opening header with the date and Torah portion for the maamar.

translations.translation: With the help of Heaven.
Shabbos Parshas Emor,
the nineteenth of Iyar,
the year 5734*

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai declares that throughout his life he was bound to the Holy One, but on his day of passing he attained a higher level of unity, being absorbed in Him.

translations.translation: Rabbi Shimon opened and said, "I am for my Beloved and His desire is upon me."
"All the days that I have been bound in this world, I have been bound in a single bond with the Holy One, blessed be He, and therefore now, 'His desire is upon me.'"
And in the continuation of the topic there,
"I would gaze every day upon this verse that is written,
'In G-d my soul shall praise itself...' and now the entire verse is fulfilled... for my soul is absorbed in Him, clings to Him, cleaves to Him..."
That throughout all the days of his life
(all the days that I have been bound in this world)
Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai was bound to the Holy One, blessed be He,
(the word "bound" is an expression of connection,
as in "and he bound it upon his hand as a sign,"
and the Targum translates, "and he bound upon his hand a crimson thread"),
for connection is specifically between two separate things,
but now,
on the day of his passing,
he reached a more elevated level,
that he became one with the Holy One, blessed be He,
"absorbed in Him."

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Although the level of being absorbed in Him was attained only on the day of passing, since he strove for it all his life, it applied to him in a general sense even during his life, with its revelation coming at the end.

translations.translation: Now, even though the level of "absorbed in Him" was reached by Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai
(only)
on the day of his passing,
nevertheless, since all his days he strove to reach this level
("I would gaze every day upon this verse"),
it is understood
that in a general sense it applies to him and he attained it
also during his lifetime,
except that the perfection of this
(the entire verse)
was fulfilled in him "now,"
on the day of his passing.
And this is also understood from what is explained in the continuation of 5666,
that the Torah study of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai was in the manner of "his Torah was his craft,"
meaning that his Torah study was in the manner of drawing down the masculine waters,
(and unlike the other Tannaim, whose study was in the manner of raising the feminine waters),
this is the concept of
("absorbed in Him")
"clings to Him,"
and this that Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai's Torah was his craft,
was throughout all the days of his life.
And one may add,
that in several discourses
the concept of "my soul is absorbed in Him" etc. is brought in continuation with "in a single bond I am bound,"
this is,
because even within the concept of "in a single bond I am bound," there is inwardly "absorbed in Him" etc.,
except that throughout all the days of his life this was not
("absorbed in Him" etc.)
in revelation,
and on the day of his passing,
when the inwardness is revealed
(the root and source)
of all matters of a person's service that he served throughout all the days of his life,
then the inwardness of "in a single bond I am bound" is revealed,
which is
(not only connection,
but also)
"absorbed in Him."
